classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the lawn diagonal as the distance needed to make two specified sides perpendicular.

content.prompt: A gardener is designing a rectangular lawn $ABCD$. If $AB=4.2\text{ m}$ and $BC=3.15\text{ m}$, how far apart should $A$ and $C$ be to ensure $\angle ABC=90^\circ$?

spec.description: Unshaded rectangle with A upper left, B upper right, C lower right and D lower left; no diagonal, measurements or angle marker. Ordinary outline uses black.
spec.mathematics: Vertex correspondence for rectangular lawn ABCD.
spec.answerVisibility: No diagonal or answer length is supplied.

answer.worked:
$AC$ must be the hypotenuse of right-angled triangle $ABC$.
$$\begin{align*}AC^2&=4.2^2+3.15^2\\AC^2&=27.5625\\AC&=\sqrt{27.5625}\\AC&=5.25\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
This distance satisfies the converse of Pythagoras’ theorem, ensuring $\angle ABC=90^\circ$.
